What the 2026 research says

Your team has AI. The work between people is still manual.

80% vs 37%

say AI improved their own productivity. Only 37% see any impact on EBIT, flat from last year.

Why it matters herePeople feel faster, but the P&L doesn’t move. The gain gets lost between people, in handoffs like the one you’re about to see.

McKinsey, The State of AI in 2026 · September 2026 · 1,719 respondents
85% vs 29%

of knowledge workers use AI at work, but only 29% have embedded it in their flow of work.

Why it matters hereMost AI sits next to the work, not inside it. A Copilot reply that never reaches the order is AI outside the flow of work.

Atlassian, State of Teams 2026 · April 2026 · 12,035 workers
69%

say most AI-assisted work happens in private sessions, not in shared spaces.

Why it matters hereWhen AI work is private, nobody else sees what changed. That’s how a customer change stays in one inbox while the job runs from another system.

Miro, State of Intelligent Collaboration 2026 · November 2026 · 9,500+ respondents · vendor survey

AI made each person faster. It didn’t make the company faster, because nobody connected the work between them.
